plan.question: Is the separable route cheaper per accepted step than the shipped route and than GMRES with the longitude preconditioner at matched achieved error on 32x64, 64x128 and 128x256?
acceptance: separable wall time and instructions below the shipped route on every grid
relative error within a factor 10 of the shipped route
mass drift <= 1e-13 on the separable route
plan.kill: slower than GMRES with the longitude preconditioner on every grid at the stage level
plan.fallback: keep the route opt-in; record the negative cells

why_a_probe: Both diagnostics run every arm inside one process, so perf stat over them counts all arms together. The probe owner_host/ks_n3_probe runs one arm per process with the helpers and settings of the test file copied verbatim (sphere grid with radius 1 and kappa 1e-2, smooth_field, the problem with an exact JVP, span [0, 1], rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-9, the separable Trusted self-reference at rtol 1e-11 and atol 1e-13; stage systems (I - sigma L) x = r with sigma = h gamma, r = noise(n, 5), GMRES restart 30, at most 3000 Arnoldi vectors, rtol 1e-10, the identity or the longitude line preconditioner; the separable solve of (z I - L) x = z r with z = 1/sigma in Trusted mode, every call planning and factoring).

whole.the_separable_route: separable-verified (SeparableMode::default(), the route VigilODE::solve_separable takes without a mode); separable-trusted is reported

stage.note: gmres-identity is reported only; a process whose GMRES fails stops at the first failure and records it (known: 128x256 at h = 0.1 exhausts 3000 Arnoldi vectors)

process: perf stat -x, -e instructions:u,cycles:u,task-clock -o <csv> -- taskset -c 8 <probe> <mode> <arm> <nt> <np> [<h>] <solves> (core 8 and its SMT sibling 20 lie outside the cores 0-5 and 12-17 to which the orchestrator's agents pin their builds)

per_solve.instructions_and_cycles: (C(1 + N) - C(1)) / N per round, cell and arm
per_solve.wall: median of the per-solve times the probe prints in the process with 1 + N solves (the process's setup and reference are outside the timed region)

order: rounds 1..3; in each round: whole cells by grid (32x64, 64x128, 128x256) with arms in the order separable-verified, separable-trusted, shipped in rounds 1 and 3 and shipped, separable-trusted, separable-verified in round 2; then stage cells by grid and h with arms gmres-longitude, separable, gmres-identity in rounds 1 and 3 and the reverse in round 2; within an arm: solves 1 then 1 + N
load_rule: the 1-minute load average is recorded before every process and no process waits for it (other projects' batch jobs held the load at 9-14 when this was written). Instruction counts decide regardless of load. A wall-time comparison is decidable if every process it uses started at load <= 3.0, or if the ratio of the medians is outside [1/3, 3] (a 3x margin); otherwise it is NOT_DECIDABLE.
statistic: per cell and metric: the median over the three rounds of the per-solve value; ratios are separable-verified / shipped (whole) and separable / gmres-longitude (stage)
consistency: within a whole cell and arm, state_fnv1a, relative_error, attempts and the counters are equal in every process with the same number of solves and in both solve counts (the solves are deterministic); a mismatch is reported and makes the cell INVALID

verdict.acceptance_per_grid: separable-verified per-solve instructions < shipped; separable-verified per-solve wall < shipped (decidable); relative_error(separable-verified) <= 10 * relative_error(shipped); mass_drift <= 1e-13 for separable-verified and separable-trusted
verdict.kill: for every grid, separable per-solve wall > gmres-longitude per-solve wall at every h (decidable comparisons only)
verdict.PASS: acceptance on every grid, no undecidable wall comparison among them, consistency holds, not KILL
verdict.KILL: kill holds (fallback: the route stays opt-in; record the negative cells)
verdict.FAIL: a decidable acceptance item fails on some grid, not KILL
verdict.NOT_DECIDABLE: no decidable failure, but some wall comparison of the acceptance is undecidable
verdict.INVALID: a consistency mismatch or a missing process
